slot.brief: Related rates: rate of change of volume/area given the rate of change of a length (sphere/cone/cube scenario).

stem: A conical vessel has liquid depth $h$ and surface radius $r=\dfrac{h}{3}$. If $h$ is increasing at $2$ cm s$^{-1}$, find the rate at which its volume increases when $h=6$ cm.

verdicts.working: V=(1/3)πr²h=πh³/27, so dV/dt=(πh²/9)(dh/dt). At h=6 and dh/dt=2, dV/dt=8π cm³ s⁻¹.

working:
$V=\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2h=\dfrac{\pi h^3}{27}$
$\dfrac{dV}{dt}=\dfrac{\pi h^2}{9}\dfrac{dh}{dt}=\dfrac{\pi(6)^2}{9}(2)=8\pi\ \text{cm}^3\,\text{s}^{-1}$

Independent check: V=(1/3)πr²h=πh³/27, so dV/dt=(πh²/9)(dh/dt). At h=6 and dh/dt=2, dV/dt=8π cm³ s⁻¹.
solution:
Using $V=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2h$ and $r=\frac{h}{3}$, we get $V=\frac{\pi h^3}{27}$.
$$\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{\pi h^2}{9}\frac{dh}{dt}=\frac{\pi(6)^2}{9}(2)=8\pi\ \text{cm}^3\,\text{s}^{-1}$$
